what.text: This page follows asylum seekers from the Dominican Republic in the United States: people who have asked for international protection and are waiting for a decision.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 15345 Dominican asylum seekers in the United States, 73.8% of all asylum seekers from the Dominican Republic.
Refugees from the Dominican Republic, a separate and much smaller group, live mostly in Canada, the United States and France.

why.text: The fact pack records no armed conflict and no dated events for the Dominican Republic, so it does not say why people left.
The main years of displacement in the data are 2024 and 2025.

when.text: UNHCR's series for this group starts in 2000 at 19 asylum seekers.
The figure is at its highest at the end of 2025.

how.text: The sources don't say which routes people took or where they live in the United States.
Asylum seekers are counted separately from refugees, as year-end totals for the United States only.
